message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph on rural interstates).
• In cities: 25–35 mph in residential areas, 35–45 mph on main streets.
• “No‑limit” roads exist in some rural counties. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster.
• Texas has a “no‑seat‑belt” law for drivers over 18. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is prohibited. | | **Alcohol & Driving** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) limit: 0.08 % for drivers ≥21.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC > 0.00 % is an offense).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | | **DUI Penalties** | • First offense: up to 90 days in jail, $1,000 fine, 6‑month license suspension.
• Subsequent offenses: harsher penalties, longer suspensions, mandatory alcohol‑abuse treatment. | | **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red light = stop; green = go; yellow = prepare to stop.
• Stop signs require a full stop.
• Yield signs give right‑of‑way to vehicles already in the intersection. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has priority.
• Pedestrians always have right‑of‑way at crosswalks.
• School buses stopping for children have absolute priority. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Passing on the right is illegal unless the left lane is occupied or a passing lane is marked. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a “no‑parking” zone (e.g., school zones) is prohibited.
• Metered parking requires payment within the posted time limit. | | **Commercial Vehicle Rules** | • Commercial drivers must hold a valid CDL.
• Hours‑of‑Service (HOS) regulations apply.
• Oversized/over‑weight vehicles need permits and may be restricted to certain routes. | | **School Bus Laws** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Drivers must not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights. | | **Towing & Vehicle Removal** | • Law enforcement can tow vehicles that are abandoned, unsafe, or blocking traffic.
• Towed vehicles must be removed within 24 hours or face additional penalties. | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Drivers must yield to emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens.
• Failure to yield can result in fines and points on the license. | | **Points System & License Suspension** | • Texas uses a points system for traffic violations.
• Accumulating 12 points in 12 months can lead to license suspension.
• Points are removed after 12 months of no violations. | | **Common Traffic Violations** | • Speeding, running red lights, reckless driving, improper lane changes, failure to yield, and driving without a valid license. | | **Legal Resources** | • Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) website for detailed statutes.
• Texas Transportation Code (Title 7, Chapter 5) contains all traffic laws.
• Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) provides driver’s handbook and penalty information. | **Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas** 1. **Always obey posted speed limits** – they’re set for safety and road conditions. 2. **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk on your phone. 3. **Keep a safe following distance** – the “two‑second rule” works well in most conditions. 4. **Check mirrors and blind spots** before changing lanes. 5. **Be extra cautious in school zones** – speeds are lower and children are present. 6. **Know your state’s DUI penalties** – they’re strict and can affect your life beyond the license. If you need more specific information (e.g., how to appeal a traffic ticket, details on a particular statute, or recent changes to the law), let me know!
